title: Count the Cost
key_points: The Lord Jesus Christ told the multitudes what following Him would cost before they signed up.
Half-started discipleship shames the name of God; He would rather we count the cost honestly first.
Carrying the cross daily means settling the question of our own life every morning, not only in a crisis.
A man who has already handed his life over has nothing left that the enemy can seize.

verse.text: And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.

scene.caption: Count the cost before the road, not on it.
scene.alt: A single cross on a hilltop path at dawn, sunlight breaking over distant hills.

title: The Witness of Stephen and the Apostles
key_points: A martyr is first of all a witness; the dying came from refusing to stop telling what was seen.
Stephen saw the Lord Jesus Christ standing to receive him and prayed forgiveness for his killers.
Nearly every apostle who ate with the risen Lord died violently for the testimony, and none recanted.
Heaven called the otherwise-unknown Antipas 'my faithful martyr,' honouring the witness the earth forgot.

verse.text: And said, Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.

scene.caption: Heaven opened to receive its faithful witness.
scene.alt: A crown resting on open ground beneath a bright, opened sky with a scroll nearby.

title: The Persecuted Church Through the Ages and Today
key_points: Rome martyred believers for refusing to call Caesar lord, yet the Church grew as it was killed.
Reformation believers were burned for owning and translating Scripture in their own tongue.
The twentieth century took more Christian lives than all prior centuries combined, and persecution continues today worldwide.
We are commanded to remember those in bonds as though we ourselves were bound with them.

verse.text: Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body.

scene.caption: Of whom the world was not worthy.
scene.alt: A broken chain beside a small steady lamp and an open Bible under a stormy sky.

title: Standing Firm When It Comes
key_points: Fear God rather than men; whichever fear is greater in you decides what you do when trouble comes.
The grace for the hour, including the words to say, is given in the hour and not before.
Prayer, fasting, and hidden holiness build the believer long before any trial arrives.
Forgiving persecutors, as Stephen did, confronts them with the living God rather than mere bravery.

verse.text: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

scene.caption: The grace for the hour is given in the hour.
scene.alt: A seven-branched lampstand burning steadily at night beneath quiet stars, with a shield beside it.

title: Faithful Unto Death: The Crown of Life
key_points: The Lord Jesus Christ promised a victor's crown of life to those faithful unto death.
Believers overcame by the blood of the Lamb, the word of their testimony, and not loving their lives unto death.
Souls under the altar are given white robes and told to rest a little season until justice is answered.
Present affliction is light and momentary set against the far more exceeding, eternal weight of glory.

verse.text: Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.

scene.caption: Faithful unto death, and He will give thee a crown of life.
scene.alt: A golden crown glowing in radiant light, with an anchor below and a dove overhead.
